full_name: Oxygen Radical Absorbance Capacity using fluorescein
main_readout: Net area under fluorescence decay curve
lipophilic_applicability: conditional via L-ORAC solvent and RMCD
physiological_relevance: moderate for peroxyl-chain chemistry but not in-vivo efficacy
main_strength: Integrates inhibition magnitude and duration against a defined chain-propagating radical
main_limitation: Strong dependence on protocol and probe kinetics; secondary reactions; limited direct relevance to absorption
major_interference: Autofluorescence; inner-filter effect; temperature; oxygen; plate position; solvent; cyclodextrin; antioxidant instability

radical_or_reagent: AAPH and fluorescein in aqueous buffer
main_strength: Well suited to soluble polyphenols and hydrophilic antioxidants
main_limitation: Under-represents poorly soluble carotenoids and tocopherols
major_interference: Solubility; pH; probe concentration; timing; fluorescence artefact

radical_or_reagent: AAPH and fluorescein with randomly methylated beta-cyclodextrin
main_strength: Provides an ORAC-family route for lipophilic molecules
main_limitation: Not numerically interchangeable with H-ORAC and depends on solubilization
major_interference: RMCD lot; acetone fraction; emulsification; solubility; fluorescence artefact
recommended_role: Primary parallel arm for lipophilic compounds
key_reference: Watanabe et al. 2016 PMID 26860561; Huang et al. 2002 PMID 11902917

main_mechanism: Quenching of a persistent organic radical
HAT_or_ET: Condition-dependent mixed ET HAT and PCET
molar_normalization_possible: yes if stoichiometric protocol and pure compound
standardization_level: moderate; AOAC method exists for specified foods
main_strength: Simple inexpensive and useful for relative reactivity in a fixed solvent
main_limitation: Steric accessibility and solvent dominate; slow reactions and endpoint choice change rank
major_interference: Sample color; turbidity; light; DPPH ageing; solvent; oxygen; reaction time
recommended_role: Secondary ET/mixed-mode screen under one protocol

full_name: ABTS radical-cation decolorization or Trolox Equivalent Antioxidant Capacity
main_mechanism: Quenching of preformed artificial radical cation
radical_or_reagent: ABTS radical cation commonly generated by persulfate
HAT_or_ET: Predominantly ET with condition-dependent HAT PCET
physiological_relevance: low-moderate because ABTS radical is artificial
cross_study_comparability: low-moderate only with same radical-generation and endpoint protocol
main_strength: Broad polarity range and convenient Trolox normalization
main_limitation: Artificial radical; multiple protocols and reaction-time sensitivity
major_interference: Sample color; radical preparation; residual oxidant; pH; solvent; slow reactions

full_name: Ferric Reducing Antioxidant Power or Ferric Reducing Ability of Plasma
possible_unit: mol Fe2+ equivalents/mol compound or mol TE/mol compound
cross_study_comparability: low-moderate only with same standard pH and time
main_strength: Fast robust measurement of reducing capacity
main_limitation: Does not measure radical chain breaking; misses slow or insoluble reducers and thiols
major_interference: Metal chelation; precipitation; sample color; pH; reaction time; Fe chemistry

lipophilic_applicability: high with suitable solvent or cyclodextrin
physiological_relevance: moderate for reducing power under near-neutral conditions
main_strength: Near-neutral pH and broad response including thiols and lipophilic antioxidants
main_limitation: Still a reducing-power assay and copper coordination can alter response
major_interference: Metal chelation; sample color; solvent; pH; complexation; reaction time

main_mechanism: Stoichiometric trapping of continuously generated peroxyl radicals
radical_or_reagent: AAPH or ABAP-derived peroxyl radicals with oxygen electrode luminol or fluorescent indicator
main_readout: Induction time oxygen consumption or inhibited signal
possible_unit: mol radicals trapped/mol compound or mol TE/mol compound
main_strength: Measures total trapping stoichiometry and chain-breaking kinetics
main_limitation: Multiple detection formats and complex calculation reduce comparability
major_interference: Luminol chemistry; oxygen control; probe choice; temperature; sample matrix

main_mechanism: Prevention of hydroxyl-radical-mediated probe oxidation often by metal chelation
radical_or_reagent: Co(II)- or Fenton-like hydroxyl-radical system and fluorescein
HAT_or_ET: Mixed prevention chelation and radical scavenging
physiological_relevance: limited because hydroxyl radical reacts diffusion-limited and assay emphasizes prevention
main_limitation: Cannot cleanly separate chelation from scavenging and hydroxyl radical selectivity is problematic
major_interference: Metal chelation; Fenton chemistry; probe damage; pH; fluorescence artefact

main_mechanism: Competition with KMBA oxidation by specified oxidants
radical_or_reagent: AAPH-derived peroxyl; Fenton-derived hydroxyl; or SIN-1-derived oxidants
possible_unit: TOSC units or relative capacity; molar form possible
physiological_relevance: moderate when oxidant identity is controlled
main_strength: Can distinguish responses to several oxidant systems
main_limitation: Specialized instrumentation and protocol-specific unit; oxidant generation chemistry is complex
major_interference: GC headspace; KMBA chemistry; radical flux; metal chemistry; matrix

radical_or_reagent: Xanthine-xanthine oxidase or other superoxide-generating systems
main_readout: Probe reduction oxidation or EPR spin signal
physiological_relevance: moderate if superoxide-specific detection and controls are used
main_strength: Can test a distinct biologically relevant ROS
main_limitation: Many probes redox-cycle and compounds may inhibit the generator rather than scavenge superoxide
major_interference: Xanthine oxidase inhibition; probe redox cycling; optical interference; metal impurities
recommended_role: Supportive only unless EPR and controls

main_readout: Probe oxidation products by LC MS fluorescence or absorbance
main_limitation: Hydroxyl radical lacks selectivity; chelation can masquerade as scavenging; assay artefacts common
major_interference: Fenton conditions; chelation; probe specificity; secondary radicals

main_mechanism: Inhibition of radical-chain oxidation in a lipid substrate
radical_or_reagent: Initiated liposome LDL emulsion or oil oxidation
HAT_or_ET: Predominantly HAT chain breaking plus partition effects
main_readout: Lag phase propagation rate oxygen uptake conjugated dienes or validated oxidation products
possible_unit: mol comparator equivalents/mol compound possible but matrix-specific
physiological_relevance: high for food-lipid functionality but model-specific
main_strength: Measures functional protection in an actual lipid phase
main_limitation: Partitioning interfacial location initiator and substrate composition can reverse rank
major_interference: Emulsion structure; oxygen; metals; light; initiator; partitioning; endpoint artefact
